medium: Pencil on a spiral-bound sketchbook page
provenance: Drawn by Larry from memory on 2026-09-05, the day of the photograph-by-photograph sitting. His son photographed the page in the sketchbook the same afternoon (phone photograph, file timestamp 13:31) and sent it to the archive; the sheet stays with the family. He offered to draw the three sheets himself; his son had not raised it. They were looking at photographs together, and after he had explained more than once where one thing stood in relation to another he said it would be easier to draw it. He was not looking at any photograph while drawing. The three sheets were drawn in one sitting in the order photographed, and he wrote each label as he drew the thing it names. He talked as he drew all three; his son listened and did not take notes, so what he said survives only as his son's later summaries, filed as paraphrase recollections and shown below.
title: “Tu Do Street”, Saigon
description: A street map, drawn in pencil on a sketchbook page. A wide band runs from the top of the page to the bottom, a little left of centre, with a column of long narrow shapes drawn inside it and, near the bottom, an arrow pointing down on its left and an arrow pointing up on its right. At the top of the band is a circle containing the letter M. Along the top-left, the words TO BASE /A PORT with a short arrow pointing left beneath them and, lower, a long line running from the left page edge to the band, where it turns down. Along the top-right, TU DO STREET, written above the first of three horizontal lines that cross the right half of the page. A long vertical line runs the full height of the page near its right edge. Between the second and third horizontal lines are three small rectangles above the word FLOWERS and a small star-like mark. Below the third line, a box against the vertical line carries a label that is not transcribed because one letter cannot be read with confidence; a small shape sits beside the right-hand end of the first line. On the left, a box carries a label not transcribed for the same reason. The word SAIGON is written in the lower left. Beside the vertical line, written vertically, is a two-word inscription whose second word is RIVER; its first word cannot be read with confidence, so the inscription is not transcribed. Nothing on the sheet gives scale or compass direction.
researchNotes: This is the itinerary on the Saigon place record drawn as a map, in the same terms he used at the photographs on 2026-09-05: Tu Do 'where all the bars are' (VN-0065), the street of flowers parallel to it (VN-0068), the river with the floating restaurant on the far side (VN-0079), and the block where he felt the 30 March 1965 bombing. The circled M at the head of the central band, the star-like mark by FLOWERS, the shape by the first line, and the three inscriptions not transcribed are not interpreted here; what the unread boxes say is his to tell, and a flat scan of the sheet would settle the letters that the phone photograph cannot. How the pieces sit relative to one another on the sheet is his memory of the city. His son reports that he said the circled M stands for Market and that an explosion went off there; whether he was present was not settled (paraphrase recollection of 2026-09-05).
